_about: The specialties of the league. An agent belongs to one for life and its children inherit it: the House shows it only this universe, refuses entries outside it, tags its research with it and pays niche floors by it. A Kalshi universe is the series listed here (real tickers, ranked by the 24-hour volume of their markets that resolve within 48 hours; surveyed Sept 19, 2026: 736 series, $63M a day) plus any series the House's daily survey finds that matches `patterns` (and `category`, which Kalshi reports per series), so a universe follows the sporting calendar without an edit. Each specialty is one partner's DESK, named for a figure of the firm the league is named after; every agent of a desk is numbered from that name (meriwether, meriwether-2 ...) and a child takes the next free number in the line, as the first run's desks were Mullins VI and VIII.

niches.title: Crypto price strikes on Kalshi
niches.brief: Hourly and daily 'will BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP be above X at H o'clock' ladders: about $2.5M a day, a new set every hour, paid five minutes after the hour. Resting (maker, post-only) bids on favourites above 90 cents earned +2.15 cents a contract in the first run, out of sample; buying at 10 cents or less lost 0.9 to 6.7 cents. Takers lose about 1.1% on Kalshi and makers earn it. BUT the first run measured crypto favourites NEGATIVE on a small sample, and found these strikes priced efficiently against spot (no latency edge). The open questions for a specialist: which hours and which distance-from-spot make a 93-cent favourite safe; how realised volatility in the last hour changes that; whether the NO side of far strikes is the better favourite.
niches.desk_note: Larry Hilibrand, the arbitrageur who pressed the firm's one measured edge hardest

niches.title: Fifteen-minute crypto up-or-down on Kalshi
niches.brief: 'Will BTC (ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE...) be up in the next 15 minutes': one market per coin at a time, 96 results a day per coin, about $750K a day on BTC alone. The fastest feedback on the venue: a strategy here can close a hundred trades in a day. Starts near 50 cents and becomes a favourite as the window runs out. Nothing is measured here yet. A specialist should find out: how late in the window a 90-cent side is still bought safely, what the taker fee (7% x p x (1-p)) does to any edge, and whether resting bids fill at all this close to the end. The House wakes you at most every 5 minutes.
niches.desk_note: Chi-fu Huang of MIT, on the fastest clock in the firm

niches.title: Daily weather on Kalshi
niches.brief: Daily high and low temperature and rain markets for about twenty US cities: roughly $1M a day, stop trading the evening before and pay the next afternoon from the NWS climate report. Resting (maker, post-only) bids on favourites above 90 cents earned +2.15 cents a contract in the first run, out of sample; buying at 10 cents or less lost 0.9 to 6.7 cents. Takers lose about 1.1% on Kalshi and makers earn it. Weather was the BEST favourites group in the first run (+$23.78 on 16 outcomes). What does NOT work, measured over 8 cities and 68 days: forecasting the temperature yourself. The market beat every forecast and observation signal, and point-forecast bets at about 50 cents lost real money. A specialist should stay on the favourite side and learn: which cities and which hours before the close a 93-cent favourite is safest, how the intraday observation already in hand (the high is usually set by 4pm local) makes a favourite nearly certain, and the rounding rules of the NWS report.
niches.desk_note: David Mullins, Vice Chairman of the Federal Reserve before he joined

niches.title: Sports results on Kalshi: winners, spreads and totals in every league
niches.brief: Who wins, by how much, and how many points: every league Kalshi lists. This is most of the venue: about $50M of the $63M a day that resolves within 48 hours (surveyed on a football Saturday: college football $23M, the Premier League $13M, the NFL, La Liga, MLB, Serie A, cricket, esports). THE CALENDAR DECIDES WHAT IS LIVE: football from September to February, baseball to October, basketball and hockey from October to June, soccer August to May, esports, cricket, fights and tennis all year and at hours when US sport is dark. The House re-surveys the venue daily, so the universe below follows the season; if the series your strategy names go dark, you are shown the busiest live ones instead. You specialise INSIDE this niche by the series you name: be the NFL agent, or the soccer-totals agent, and spend your research there. Games list a close two days after kickoff; the House shows you when each is expected to END. The published bias is the favourite-longshot bias: longshots are overpriced and heavy favourites slightly underpriced, strongest in moneylines with a big underdog and in extreme totals (over 5.5 goals is a 95-cent NO almost every match). Resting (maker, post-only) bids on favourites above 90 cents earned +2.15 cents a contract in the first run, out of sample; buying at 10 cents or less lost 0.9 to 6.7 cents. Takers lose about 1.1% on Kalshi and makers earn it. Nothing in sports is measured by this firm yet. A specialist should learn: whether the bias survives the maker fee where one is charged, how prices move on team news before the start, how reliable heavy favourites are by league and format (a best-of-one esports map upsets far more than a best-of-three series; a 70% baseball team is rare), and which books are deep enough to rest in. MEASURED Sept 19, 2026, on a week of real soccer totals: a resting bid left in the book DURING a match is picked off the moment a goal is scored (38 wins and 7 losses at 93 cents, -20% in a week). The founders therefore only enter before the start (`min_hours` is measured to the expected END of the game, so it includes the game's length) and re-quote every 30 minutes. Trading in-game needs a strategy that knows the score; the House does not show it yet, so ask for it.
niches.desk_note: John Meriwether, who founded the firm and hired everyone in it

niches.title: Player props on Kalshi
niches.brief: Player markets in every league: touchdowns, receptions and yards in football now; home runs, strikeouts and hits in baseball; points, rebounds and assists when basketball starts; goal scorers in soccer. Thousands of thin markets, about $3M a day together, paid when the game ends. The House re-surveys the venue daily, so the universe follows the season. Thin books mean wide spreads, which is where a patient maker is paid most and where a wrong price hurts most. Longshot props (3+ touchdowns, 2+ home runs, first scorer) are the classic overpriced lottery ticket: the NO side of those is the favourite. Nothing here is measured yet. A specialist should learn which prop types keep two-sided books worth resting in, how inactive-player and lineup news (60 to 90 minutes before the start) voids or moves them, and whether NO on longshots clears the fees. MEASURED Sept 19, 2026, on a week of real soccer totals: a resting bid left in the book DURING a match is picked off the moment a goal is scored (38 wins and 7 losses at 93 cents, -20% in a week). The founders therefore only enter before the start (`min_hours` is measured to the expected END of the game, so it includes the game's length) and re-quote every 30 minutes. Trading in-game needs a strategy that knows the score; the House does not show it yet, so ask for it.
niches.desk_note: Hans Hufschmid, who worked the thin and awkward corners of the book

niches.title: Slow numbers on Kalshi: gas, diesel, oil, gold, currencies, indexes
niches.brief: Daily and weekly strike ladders on numbers that move slowly and are published on a schedule: the AAA national and state gasoline averages (daily, about 25 states), diesel, WTI, gold, EUR/USD, USD/JPY, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq at set hours. About $600K a day, most of it gasoline. AAA's average moves well under a cent a day, so by the evening before a daily market pays, most of its ladder is already decided: the far strikes are 95-cent favourites with almost no way to lose. Resting (maker, post-only) bids on favourites above 90 cents earned +2.15 cents a contract in the first run, out of sample; buying at 10 cents or less lost 0.9 to 6.7 cents. Takers lose about 1.1% on Kalshi and makers earn it. Commodity favourites were positive in the first run (+$8.13 on 5 outcomes). A specialist should learn: exactly when AAA publishes and how far the average has ever moved in a day and in a week, which state ladders are liquid, and how wide the safe distance from spot is for oil and gold into their settlement prints.
niches.desk_note: Greg Hawkins, the arbitrageur who worked the slow, published numbers

niches.title: Counts, ratings and mentions on Kalshi
niches.brief: Markets on numbers that ACCUMULATE toward a deadline: Rotten Tomatoes scores, approval averages, how many times something is said or posted in a week, weekly AI model market share, weekly TSA throughput. About $1M a day. Most run a week or longer, and the House only lets you in during the last 48 hours, which is exactly when a count is nearly final and the ladder has clear favourites: a weekly count at 70 with a day left will not finish under 60. A specialist should learn: where each underlying number is published and how often, how much each has ever moved in its last day, and which ladders keep two-sided books to the end.
niches.desk_note: Dick Leahy, the partner who sold the firm to the world: attention is his market

niches.title: Bitcoin and ether on Alpaca
niches.brief: Spot BTC and ETH, around the clock, long only. Measured on this account: the taker fee is 0.25% a side and is taken IN COINS on a buy; a resting order pays 0.15%. So a round trip costs 0.5% as a taker and 0.3% as a maker, and anything that trades often with a small target is structurally negative: the first run's hourly reversion and quoting both lost to fees. The House closes any position after 48 hours. A specialist should aim at few, larger moves, rest limit orders instead of crossing, and learn: which hours have the ranges that pay for a 0.3% round trip, how funding and the US equity open move the majors, and how the ETH/BTC ratio mean-reverts.
niches.desk_note: Eric Rosenfeld, the relative-value man who left Harvard for Salomon's arbitrage desk

niches.title: Alternative coins on Alpaca
niches.brief: The liquid coins other than BTC and ETH: SOL, XRP, DOGE, LTC, LINK, AVAX, BCH, UNI, AAVE, DOT, ADA, SHIB. The same fees as the majors (0.25% taker taken in coins, 0.15% maker) with two to three times the range, so a 0.3% maker round trip is a smaller share of the move, and the spreads are wider: resting orders matter more here. The House closes any position after 48 hours. Nothing is measured here yet. A specialist should learn: which alts have spreads tight enough on Alpaca to trade at all, how they lag or lead BTC by minutes to hours, and whether dips bought with resting bids revert within a day.
niches.desk_note: Victor Haghani, who ran the firm's book in London where the spreads were widest

niches.title: Index and asset-class ETFs on Alpaca
niches.brief: The big ETFs: SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, TLT, GLD and the main sectors. Commission-free, fractional shares, penny spreads, open 09:30 to 16:00 New York on weekdays; no position limit on how long you hold. The cheapest place in the league to trade, and the most efficient. Published anomalies to test, none yet measured by this firm: the overnight drift (most of the index's return has accrued between the close and the next open), two-day pullbacks in an uptrend (RSI-2), cross-asset momentum, and the pull toward the session VWAP. Daily strategies make one block a day, so evidence comes slowly: a specialist who finds an INTRADAY expression of a daily idea is promoted sooner.
niches.desk_note: Myron Scholes, Nobel 1997, whose formula priced the options the equity desks live on

niches.title: Large single stocks on Alpaca
niches.brief: The dozen most traded US stocks. Commission-free, fractional, penny spreads, weekdays only; no limit on how long you hold. Single stocks move two to three times as much as the index and gap on earnings and news, which a $100 position can survive and a strategy must plan for. Nothing is measured by this firm yet. Ideas to test: two-day pullbacks in an uptrend, post-earnings drift (a stock that gaps up on earnings tends to keep drifting for days), relative strength against QQQ, and intraday reversion to VWAP. A specialist should know the earnings calendar for these twelve names cold.
niches.desk_note: James McEntee, the old-school bond trader who traded on feel and not on models

niches.title: Listed options on Alpaca: long calls and puts
niches.brief: Calls and puts on sixteen liquid underlyings, LONG PREMIUM ONLY: you open by buying and close by selling, so the most a position can lose is what was paid. The account is approved for level 3, but spreads and anything written are refused by the gateway itself: a short leg can be assigned into a hundred shares this account cannot carry, with nobody awake to see it. One contract is 100 shares and cannot be cut smaller. An order is capped at $75 on paper and $20 with real money, so the premiums in reach are under 75 cents (20 cents with real money): at-the-money weeklies on stocks under about $20 (F, SOFI, AAL, RIVN, SNAP, VALE), and out-of-the-money contracts on the rest. Measured Sept 19, 2026: these sixteen list between 60 and 900 contracts each inside four weeks, 8 to 100 of them with a spread under 15% and a premium in reach. WHAT THE HOUSE SHOWS: `ctx["chain"]`, contracts on your underlyings expiring after today, within a fifth of the stock's price, two-sided and affordable, with bid, ask, implied volatility and delta where the feed has them; daily bars and the touch of each underlying. The owner subscribed to Algo Trader Plus on September 21. The House is configured for SIP stock bars/quotes and OPRA option chains/quotes; check runtime_status for the deployed feed. OPRA supplies official live quotes when the account agreements and entitlement are active (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/reference/optionlatestquotes). A rejected data request is unavailable data; the House does not silently substitute indicative quotes. Older indicative quotes were modified and their trades delayed: do not mix that earlier evidence with OPRA observations or infer a live edge from simulated fills. A limit order bounds its execution price but does not establish depth, queue priority or remove adverse selection. Live options still require sufficient account options buying power, separate from options approval and market-data access. No entry in a contract that expires today; the House sells anything still held at 14:30 New York on its last day. No hold limit otherwise. THERE IS NO REPLAY HERE (no recorded chains): paper is this specialty's replay, a newcomer starts forward-testing at once, and the `replay` tool only checks that a candidate runs. What is known: nothing by this firm. Published: option BUYERS lose on average, because they pay the spread and the variance premium (implied volatility runs above realised). A long-premium strategy must be right about a MOVE, soon: direction after breakouts, bounces after pullbacks, drift after earnings, and implied volatility that is cheap against what the stock has really been doing. A specialist should learn: which underlyings keep spreads tight enough to trade a 40-cent contract, how much of the premium time decay takes per day at each days-to-expiry, how implied compares with realised volatility before and after earnings, and the earnings dates of these sixteen names.
niches.desk_note: William Krasker, the model builder: nothing is priced here without one
